page_title: How to Create an Organisation with Geographic Scope
page_description: Learn how to set up a new organisation in Public Digit and configure geographic scope for your voting structure.
page_keywords: organisation creation, geographic scope, committee structure, online voting setup
hero_subtitle: Set up your organisation for secure, democratic voting
section_1_intro: Before creating an organisation, make sure you have:
section_1_requirement_1: A Public Digit account (sign up if you haven't already)
section_1_requirement_2: Basic information about your organisation (name, contact email)
section_1_requirement_3: Understanding of your committee structure (flat or geographical)
section_1_step_1: Navigate to the Create Organisation page
section_1_step_1_desc: Click the 'Create Organisation' button in your dashboard or go directly to /my-organisations/create
section_2_intro: Fill in the essential details about your organisation:
section_2_field_name_desc: Enter a memorable name for your organisation (minimum 3 characters). This will appear in emails and voting pages.
section_2_field_name_example: Example: NRNA Bavaria, Tech Community Nepal, Student Government Board
section_2_field_email_desc: The email address where voting members and officers can reach you. This will be public on your organisation page.
section_2_field_representative_desc: The name of the primary contact person or head of the organisation.
section_2_field_languages_desc: Select which languages your members will see during voting. You can choose English, German, and/or Nepali.
section_2_field_logo_desc: Upload a professional logo (PNG, JPG, SVG, or WebP, max 2 MB). This will appear on all election materials.
section_3_intro: Choose how voters are eligible for your elections:
section_3_option_full_desc: Voters must be formal members with paid fees. Best for organisations with membership tracking and annual dues.
section_3_option_election_desc: Any registered user can vote without membership requirements. Best for simple elections or open communities.
section_3_tip: 📌 Tip: This setting determines who can be invited to vote in your elections. You can change this later.
section_4_title: 4. Committee Structure: The Foundation of Your Organisation
section_4_intro: Your committee structure determines how your organisation is governed and how elections are conducted.
section_4_flat_desc: Choose this if your organisation has one central committee that manages everything with no parent-child hierarchy.
section_4_flat_use_case_2: Small teams where everyone votes together
section_4_flat_use_case_3: Organisations that don't need regional divisions
section_4_flat_example: Example: A local book club might have one committee making all decisions.
section_4_flat_result: Result: All elections show the same candidates to all voters. No regional filtering.
section_4_geo_desc: Choose this if your organisation spans multiple regions and needs a hierarchical structure.
section_4_geo_level_1_desc: The broadest geographic division (Europe, Asia, Africa, etc.)
section_4_geo_level_2_desc: Countries within continents (Germany, Austria, Nepal, etc.)
section_4_geo_level_3_desc: States, provinces, or districts within countries (Bavaria, Karnataka, etc.)
section_4_geo_example: Example: NRNA (Non-Resident Nepali Association) has members worldwide. They might elect delegates at the country level who then vote in continental committees.
section_5_intro: After selecting 'Geographical Committees', you'll configure your geographic scope.
section_5_note: ⚠️ Important: Geographic configuration cannot be changed after creation. Choose carefully.
section_5_worldwide_desc: All countries are included. Members from any country can vote in elections.
section_5_worldwide_example: A global tech community that operates in all countries
section_5_worldwide_result: All voters see all candidates. No geographic filtering applied.
section_5_multi_desc: You specify 2 or more countries where your organisation operates. Voters and elections are limited to these countries.
section_5_multi_example: NRNA Germany & Austria: Select Germany, Austria, and Switzerland as allowed countries
section_5_multi_step_2: Search and select each country you want to include (minimum 2)
section_5_multi_step_3: The selection counter shows how many countries you've selected
section_5_multi_result: Voters from selected countries can vote. Regional posts show only candidates from that voter's country.
section_5_single_desc: Your organisation operates in exactly one country. All elections and members are limited to that country.
section_5_single_example: CDU Bayern (Bavarian Christian Democratic Union operates only in Germany)
section_5_single_step_1: Select your base country from the dropdown
section_5_single_result: All voters must be from the selected country. System prevents voting from other countries.
section_5_sub_desc: Your organisation operates in one specific region or state within a country.
section_5_sub_example: Bavaria Diaspora Association operates only in the Bavaria region of Germany
section_5_sub_step_2: The system automatically loads regions/states for that country
section_5_sub_step_3: Select the specific region where your organisation operates
section_5_sub_result: Voters are restricted to the selected region. Maximum geographic specificity.
section_6_intro: Before submitting, review all your choices:
section_6_checklist_1: ✓ Organisation name is clear and memorable
section_6_checklist_2: ✓ Contact email is correct and monitored
section_6_checklist_3: ✓ Committee structure matches your governance needs
section_6_checklist_4: ✓ Geographic scope is appropriate for your members
section_6_checklist_5: ✓ You understand these choices are permanent
section_6_final_note: Click 'Create Organisation' to proceed. You'll become the owner and can start inviting members.
section_7_intro: Once your organisation is created, you can:
section_7_action_1: Invite members to join your organisation
section_7_action_4: Set up election officers and administrators
section_8_q1: Can I change my organisation's structure after creation?
section_8_a1: No. Committee structure and geographic scope are permanent. Choose carefully during setup.
section_8_q2: What if I'm not sure about my geographic scope?
section_8_a2: Start with 'Worldwide' or 'Single Country' — these are more flexible. You can always create a new organisation if needed.
section_8_q3: How many members can my organisation have?
section_8_a3: No hard limit. Public Digit supports organisations from 10 to 100,000+ members.
section_8_q4: Can I use different languages for different elections?
section_8_a4: Yes. You select organisation-wide languages during setup, but each election can use a subset of those languages.
section_8_a5: A unique code sent to each eligible voter that grants access to voting. One code = one voter.
